name: Mirrored sunglass lenses

lead: Mirrored lenses are tinted sunglass lenses with a metallic, partly reflective coating on the outside. The coating hides the wearer's eyes and gives the glasses a distinctive look, which is why the style is common on aviators and sport frames.

Beyond style, the coating bounces some light away before it enters the lens, which helps in bright conditions. Coating colour is independent of tint, so the same lens can be paired with different mirror colours.

paras: People pick a frame shape, a tint and a mirror colour (for example silver, blue or gold). Mirrored lenses are worn as an accessory to change the overall look, often with aviator or wrap styles, and in bright outdoor settings.

The coating does not necessarily block UV well, so UV protection should be checked separately from the mirror finish. Because the eyes are hidden, some wearers use mirrored lenses to avoid eye contact, which can change how approachable a person appears.

angle.text: The mirror finish changes the visible look of the glasses and conceals the eyes, so wearers use it to adjust the style and attitude of their appearance. Colour choice adds further variety.

lead: Mirrored sunglass lenses, also called mirrorshades, have a metallic, partially reflective coating applied to the outer surface of a tinted lens [1].

The coating deflects some light before it reaches the lens, lowering transmission and helping in bright conditions. Its colour is independent of the tint beneath, so a gray lens can have a blue mirror and a brown lens a silver one [1]. Mirrored lenses hide the eyes more effectively than plain tints [1].

As a style item, mirrored coatings are often seen on aviators, which Bausch and Lomb introduced in 1936 for US military pilots and which are made in mirrored, colored and wrap-around versions [1]. On T Nation, forum members have discussed sunglass brands and lens types, including mirrored and polarized options, in the context of style and sport [2][3].
infobox: Reflects part of incoming light; hides eyes

paras: A thin metallic layer on the outside of a tinted lens reflects some light, so less reaches the eye. This is useful in bright light, and the layer is described as not heating up in sunlight [1].

T Nation threads treat sunglasses as both gear and fashion. One forum user mentions owning several Oakley, Wiley X and Costa pairs, and others discuss shutter shades and tinted or polarized lenses [2][3][4].
A mirror finish does not necessarily block UV as well as other lens treatments, so UV rating is a separate property of the lens [1].

timeline.event: Bausch and Lomb introduces the aviator design for US military pilots; it later appears in mirrored versions [1].
